forecaster_note: Still some longer and mid-period S swell and enough for chest to maybe head high surf at south magnets - smaller elsewhere. It should be clean through the earlier morning, but there's another S wind switch due. Current timing is putting it about 9/10am through Sydney. Once it's through we're looking at lumpy onshore conditions. — Anthony Spinks, Surfline

wind.summary: NW offshore 12kph now, WNW 20kph by 9am — then a S change at 35kph gusting 45 from midday.

shark.summary: No shark detections at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly in the past 24h. Nearest: one SLS drone sighting at Freshwater Beach (between Curl Curl and Manly) at 7:22am Sun 20 Sep — about 23h ago. Feed confirmed live: 72 detections statewide in the last 24h.

days.label: Today
days.note: Dawn patrol or nothing. NW offshore holds until about 9am, then the S change lands at 35kph gusting 45 and shuts it down for the day. Long Reef is the clear pick — it's holding 4–5ft off a dead-S 182° swell that Dee Why barely sees.

dee-why.window: Dawn to 9am. NW offshore 12–20kph, then it's over.
alerts: Dead-S swell at 182° — wraps badly into Dee Why, you're getting about half of Long Reef's size

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: The Point is your frontside right — but at 182° the swell is running straight past it. Sit wide on the bank off the Point rather than the corner; the 15s long-period pulses are the only ones bending in.

long-reef.window: Dawn to 9am — the standout of the four this morning.

tip.label: Frontside, and twice the size
tip.text: Long Reef is exposed to the dead-S angle the others are shadowed from — 4–5ft here versus 2–4 at Dee Why. Frontside rights off the point with 82% consistency and 704kJ on the peak sets. Go here.

tip.label: Both ways off the peak
tip.text: Beachbreak, so take the frontside rights off the north side of each peak. Rated fair-good at 6am but drops to poor by 9 — this is a first-light-only call.

manly.window: Skip it. Knee to thigh at best.
alerts: Most S-shadowed of the four — barely registering this swell

tip.label: Not today
tip.text: North Steyne is the wrong end of the beach for a 182° swell. Nothing here worth the drive when Long Reef is double the size.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Twice the size and 91% consistency, but S onshore 13–16kph all morning makes it lumpy and sectiony. The wind drops to 4kph by 6pm — the last hour of light is the play.

dee-why.window: Late arvo — wind eases to 4kph by 6pm for a glass-off.
alerts: S onshore 148–153° at 13–16kph through the whole morning

long-reef.window: Biggest of the four. Wait for the evening glass-off.
alerts: Overhead-plus and onshore — heavy, not clean
Most exposed to the onshore of the three beachies

manly.window: Most sheltered — the cleanest option on a lumpy day.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Two completely different days. Saturday is tiny and clean — 2–3ft with light NW offshore all morning. Sunday 27 is the event: a 16.9ft @ 11s dead-S groundswell arrives with light offshore until about 11am, then 35kph S. Long Reef 8–11ft with 20ft sets. Expert-only, and a genuine gun day.

dee-why.window: Sat 6–11am small and clean. Sun dawn–11am for the big S.
alerts: Sun 27: 16.9ft @ 11s from 179° — dead-S again, so Dee Why under-performs but still overhead-plus

long-reef.window: Sunday dawn to 11am. 8–11ft with light offshore — gun territory.
alerts: Sunday is expert-only — 20ft sets and 6277kJ on the peak

curl-curl.window: Sat clean and small; Sunday likely closing out.
alerts: Sun 27 max sets to 18ft — probably unsurfable beachbreak

manly.window: Sunday's safest call — the S shadow keeps it rideable at 4–6ft.
